system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present and the encodings (GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic) are consistent with the page counts. Two fixable problems remain. First, both texts are far over the 1-page handset limit (en 3 pages, ar 6 pages). Second, neither text contains a protective action, so the first page carries the hazard but no instruction.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE handset limit of one cell broadcast page. English is 190 GSM-7 characters over 3 pages; Arabic is 234 UCS-2 characters over 6 pages. Only the first page can be relied on to be read, so most of the content risks being lost or split.
objections.fix: Cut each language to a single page: about 93 characters or fewer in GSM-7 for English, and about 41 characters or fewer in UCS-2 for Arabic. Keep only the hazard, area, time window and one action, and drop the source line and full dates. If Arabic cannot fit hazard plus action in one UCS-2 page, put the action first and refer that to the issuing authority.

objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic text contains any protective action for recipients. They describe only the fog, area, time and source, so the first page carries the hazard but not the action.
objections.fix: Add a short action at the start of the message in both languages, for example 'Avoid driving; if you must, slow down and use low beams', with an equivalent Arabic wording. Place it in the first page, right after the hazard.
